questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Arbitrary**.

• The word **"Disorderly"** means lacking organization, order, or arrangement; chaotic or untidy. (अव्यवस्थित)
 
 
• **Example: **The desk was cluttered and disorderly, making it hard to find anything.
 
 
 
• **"Arbitrary"** refers to something that is random, not based on any reason, order, or system; it can also mean capricious or unpredictable. (मनमाना)
 
 
• **Example: **The manager made an arbitrary decision to change the work schedule without consulting anyone.
 
 
 
• Hence, the synonym for **'Disorderly'** is **'Arbitrary'**.

• **Example: **His deliberate actions showed careful planning.
 
 
 
• **Systematic** (संगठित): Following a fixed plan or system; methodical.
 
 
• **Example:** The systematic arrangement of files made it easy to locate documents.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence from active to passive voice:

The lecturer might have been teaching abstract algebra for hours.

options.text: Abstract algebra might have taught by the lecturer.
Abstract algebra might have been being taught by the lecturer.
Abstract algebra might be teaching by the lecturer.
Abstract algebra might have had been taught by the lecturer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence. 
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The lecturer might have been teaching abstract algebra for hours." 
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "abstract algebra" at the beginning. 
 
• Change the active verb form "might have been teaching" to "might have been being taught" (past perfect continuous passive). 
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the lecturer." 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Abstract algebra might have been being taught by the lecturer for hours."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: **"Abstract algebra might have taught by the lecturer." – Missing the correct form of the verb "been being." 
 
• **Option 3: **"Abstract algebra might be teaching by the lecturer." – Incorrect form of tense and structure. 
 
• **Option 4: **"Abstract algebra might have had been taught by the lecturer." – Grammatically incorrect and redundant.

questions.question:
Select the correct direct speech conversion of the sentence below:

The musician remarked that, were the harmony shifted upward, the effect might weaken.

options.text: The musician said, “If the harmony was shifted upward, the effect will weaken.”
The musician said, “Were the harmony shifted upward, the effect might weaken.”
The musician said, “The effect weakens if harmony had shifted.”
The musician said, “Had harmony shifted upward, the effect must weaken.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The musician remarked that, were the harmony shifted upward, the effect might weaken.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"were the harmony shifted" remains "Were the harmony shifted" in direct speech.**
 
 
• Since the sentence is in subjunctive mood, the verb structure "were shifted" remains unchanged.
 
• The auxiliary verb "might" is retained to reflect possibility.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "remarked"
 
• Converted to: "said," which is neutral and suitable for reporting direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Were" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**The musician said, “Were the harmony shifted upward, the effect might weaken.*”

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "If the harmony was shifted upward, the effect will weaken." 

 
 
• Incorrect tense: "was" and "will" do not align with the subjunctive mood or possibility.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The effect weakens if harmony had shifted." 
 
 
• Incorrect conditional structure: "if harmony had shifted" does not reflect the subjunctive mood.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Had harmony shifted upward, the effect must weaken." 
 
 
• Incorrect modal verb: "must" changes the meaning from possibility to certainty.

questions.question:
A sentence is given in direct speech. Choose the correct indirect form:

She said, “I have completed the assignment.”

options.text: She said that she completed the assignment.
She said that she had completed the assignment.
She said that she has completed the assignment.
She said that she was completing the assignment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she had completed the assignment.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Present perfect tense ("have completed") becomes past perfect tense ("had completed").**
 
 
• When converting from direct to indirect speech, the tense is shifted back in time if the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun "I" becomes "she".**
 
 
• Pronouns in reported speech are adjusted based on the subject of the reporting verb.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Direct: She said, "I have completed the assignment."
 
• Indirect: She said that she had completed the assignment.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The conjunction "that" is added to connect the reporting clause and the reported clause.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *She said that she had completed the assignment.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** She said that she completed the assignment.
 
 
• Incorrect tense. The past simple tense "completed" does not match the present perfect tense in the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** She said that she has completed the assignment.
 
 
• Incorrect tense. "Has completed" is present perfect tense and does not match the shift to past perfect tense required in reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** She said that she was completing the assignment.
 
 
• Incorrect tense and meaning. "Was completing" (past continuous) does not match "have completed" (present perfect).
 
 
</ul
